area: Task 28 Phase 2 — source-brand surface recon: detection, the unclearable blocker, real surface counts from the accepted linear.app/stripe.com templates, and the bake-time whole-asset rewrite seam (incl. the RSC flight payload)
findings: 1A DETECTION — src/release/brand-scan.ts (GED-F, detector only). `scanBrandSurfaces` (brand-scan.ts:284-450) reads THREE evidence sources and writes nothing. (i) brand-scan.ts:306-336 delegates to `scanRuntimeTemplateSurfaces` (src/content-injection/brand-surfaces.ts:251-321), which walks `<templateRunDir>/app/reconstruction-data/route-map.json` → `pages/*.json`, both viewports, stack-pop order, `v` before `p`; every hit carries route+viewport+`data-wr-node` id+pageFile+pointer `desktop.doc[nXXXXXX].v`. (ii) brand-scan.ts:338-392 reads the content run's `report/brand-leak.json`, SKIPPING every entry with `slotKey === null` (brand-scan.ts:362) to avoid double-counting the CR8 surface-scoped entries. (iii) brand-scan.ts:394-424 reads `<productionBuildDir>/report/qa.json` `.brandSurfaceCensus.byRoute[].bodyAnchorIdentity`. Output: `BrandSurfaceReport` (brand-scan.ts:81-105) with exact `counts` per surface plus a per-surface-capped (25, brand-scan.ts:278) `findings` sample. `GED_F_NEUTRALIZATION_DEFAULT = false` (brand-scan.ts:52) and is asserted false by scripts/smoke-content-injection.ts:2268-2270 (27.brand.8), with 27.brand.11 (smoke-content-injection.ts:2291) asserting every input byte AND mtime is unchanged by a scan.

1B DETECTION — the surface vocabulary and the Task-27 SVG additions. `BRAND_SURFACES` is a closed 14-value list (brand-surfaces.ts:33-48). The Task-27 additions live in `scanInlineSvgMarkup` (brand-surfaces.ts:111-136) over the RuntimeElementNode `v` markup: `SVG_ARIA_LABEL = /\baria-label\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"/g` (:102) → `svg-aria-label`; `SVG_SYMBOL_ID = /<symbol\b[^>]*?\bid\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"/g` (:103) matched through `firstBrandTokenInIdentifier` (:92-100), which splits camel humps so `LinearAi` matches; `SVG_TEXTUAL = /<(text|title)\b[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/\1>/g` (:104) → `svg-text`. `scanElementProps` (:155-201) covers href/src/poster/action + srcset → `source-url`, `alt` → `image-alt`, `aria-label` → `aria-label`. Brand tokens come from `brandTokensFromHost` (:69-76): host first label + `-`/`_` parts ≥4 chars, all ≥3 chars — `linear.app` → ["linear"], `stripe.com` → ["stripe"]. Word-boundary matching only (`containsBrandToken` :79-81).

1C DETECTION — src/production/brand-census.ts (Phase 1 CR7 extraction). `censusServedHtml` (brand-census.ts:52-93) censuses ONE served/exported HTML document into 8 numeric axes (`BrandSurfaceCounts` :25-34). It reuses `scanInlineSvgMarkup` over `/<svg\b[\s\S]*?<\/svg>/gi` blocks (:42,:67-74), counts aria-label OUTSIDE svg separately (:76-79), img `alt` (:80-82), any href/src/poster/action on the source host (:83-85), body anchors (:86), and visible text after stripping `<script>` and tags (:87-91). Two callers: src/production/bake.ts:282-304 over THIS bake's exported route HTML (`BakeReport.brand`, measuredOn `static-export-route-html`), and src/production/qa.ts:314 over the served package fetched by HTTP → `ProductionQaReport.brandSurfaceCensus`, written to `report/qa.json` by src/release/stages.ts:337-344 — which brand-scan.ts:398-417 reads back. Both are MEASUREMENTS, never assertions; production/qa.ts:75 explicitly refuses to make an `=== 0` check out of them.

2A THE BLOCKER — there are TWO brand requirement kinds and only one blocks. `source-brand-asset` is release-blocking by SEVERITY_POLICY (src/release/types.ts:566-569: "§19: visible source-brand content must be 0 — inline-SVG marks are outside the asset layer"). `brand-leak` defaults to high-value (types.ts:600-609) and is escalated per-finding by `brandFindingSeverity` (brand-scan.ts:251-260), which returns `release-blocking` ONLY when policy.canBlock AND `finding.slotKey !== null` AND `finding.origin === "injected-value"` — i.e. only `visible-text` (the only canBlock:true row that is slot-bound; brand-scan.ts:132-139). Every SVG surface is canBlock:false with the reason stated in code (svg-aria-label brand-scan.ts:203-210: "NEW in Task 27 … It has NO slot binding and no bake-time rewriter yet, so blocking it would repeat the source-brand-asset dead end"; svg-symbol-id :211-218; image-logo :173-180 defers to `replacement-image`/`source-brand-asset`).

2B THE BLOCKER — the single unclearable requirement, and its exact clearing logic. Created at src/release/collect.ts:513-551: `requirementId: "source-brand-inline-svg"`, `kind: "source-brand-asset"`, `sourceStage: "template"`, emitted whenever `inventoryManifest.counts.inlineSvgEntries > 0` (collect.ts:514). `releaseBlockers` (src/release/requirements.ts:237-244) filters `severity === "release-blocking" && status !== "resolved" && status !== "not-applicable"`, and `deriveReleaseState` (src/release/gate.ts:37-49) requires `blockers.length === 0` for PRODUCTION_READY. THREE and only three paths could change its status: (a) `resolved` via `matchResolutionToRequirements` (requirements.ts:42-131) — the assets branch (:84-92) can only ever produce the ids `og-image`, `organization-logo`, `replacement-image-<inventoryId>`; NO resolution field in the whole matcher can produce the id `source-brand-inline-svg`, so `resolved` is structurally unreachable; (b) `accepted-limitation` via `acknowledgements` (requirements.ts:120-129, 216-222) — which still blocks, by the comment at requirements.ts:235-236 ("`accepted-limitation` still blocks indexable production (spec §7: blockers must be RESOLVED)") and the filter at :241; (c) `not-applicable` via the carry-forward at requirements.ts:187-193, which fires ONLY when the requirement is no longer collected — i.e. only when `counts.inlineSvgEntries` reaches 0. That is the whole clearing surface: the blocker clears iff the ASSET INVENTORY reports zero inline-SVG entries. Task 27's verdict is exactly right and nothing has changed.

2C THE BLOCKER — its count is not the brand problem, measured. `inlineSvgEntries` is `entries.filter((e) => e.url === null).length` (src/assets/run.ts:172) — EVERY inline SVG, icons included. Real number for linear.app: data/linear.app/asset-inventories/2026-08-25T23-19-27-365Z/manifest.json `counts.inlineSvgEntries = 207` (entries 448, urlEntries 241). Brand-carrying inline-SVG hosts in the same lineage's template IR: 64 (measured, §3B below), of which only 4 are real brand marks and 1 is a 264-symbol icon sprite. The blocker therefore overstates the brand surface by ~3.2×, and `buildPreviewBlockers` (src/production/run.ts:143-147, fed by run.ts:283) reports the same 207-class number as the preview blocker's evidence. Any Phase-2 blocker must be counted from brand-carrying hosts, not from the inventory total.

3A SURFACES — cross-validation: the template IR counts EXACTLY reproduce the production bake census. Independently walking data/linear.app/recon-templates/2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z/app/reconstruction-data (8 routes × {desktop,mobile}) and counting distinct (route, viewport, data-wr-node) hosts gives: svg aria-label brand 48, svg <symbol id> brand 16 hosts carrying 32 brand ids, img alt brand 14, element aria-label brand 2, svg <text>/<title> brand 0. The bake census of the newest real build (data/linear.app/production-builds/2026-08-27T09-38-59-704Z/report/bake-report.json `.brand.census`, 8 routes) reports: svgAriaLabel 48, svgSymbolId 32, imageAlt 14, ariaLabel 2, svgText 0, sourceUrl 76, visibleText 342, bodyAnchorIdentity 0. Every axis matches. CONSEQUENCE: a rewrite applied to the runtime IR reaches exactly the surfaces the census measures — there is no gap between the seam and the metric.

3B SURFACES — enumerated by class, real counts and real examples (linear.app template 2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z, 8 routes; stripe.com template 2026-08-26T22-38-06-075Z, 20 routes). (a) SOURCE-BRAND LOGO: ZERO in every accepted template. linear has 436 hosts, stripe 1710; grepping `"src"` values for /logo|brand|mark/ finds only THIRD-PARTY customer logos (stripe: `logo-FoxSports-…` ×96, `logo-Kajabi-…` ×12; linear: none at all), and nextjs.org / domainchecker.co.kr templates have none. Phase 2 CANNOT get an `` source logo from real data; that fixture case must be synthetic and must be labelled as such. (b) INLINE

3C SURFACES — WHAT IS DETERMINISTICALLY REPLACEABLE AS A WHOLE HOST (the decisive measurement). Normalizing away the compiler-stamped `data-wr-node`/`class`/`id` and hashing the remaining `v` markup: linear's 64 brand-carrying hosts collapse to FIVE distinct markups, stripe's 108 to FOUR. linear: (i) ×16, 3104 B, `<svg height="22" viewBox="0 0 400 100" fill="currentColor" size="22" color="currentColor" aria-label="Linear">` — the header wordmark, node n000017 on all 8 routes × both viewports; (ii) ×16, 844 B, `<svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="currentColor" aria-label="Linear Logo" …>` (e.g. / desktop n002610); (iii) ×14, 860 B, same glyph with `width="20%" fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)" aria-label="Linear logo"` (/changelog desktop n003198); (iv) ×2, 824 B, same glyph at 13×13 `fill="#E2E4E6"` (/ desktop n000130); (v) ×16, 183,963 B, the ICON SPRITE `<svg width="0" height="0"><defs><symbol id="Accessibility">…` at / desktop n002769. stripe: ×100 1333 B `<svg viewBox="0 0 60 25"><title>Stripe logo</title>…` (/cookie-settings desktop n007080); ×4 1962 B `aria-label="Stripe logo"` (n000010 on the careers routes); ×2 1965 B same mark `fill="#031323"` (/ desktop n000010); ×2 4854 B `aria-label="Stripe Sessions logo"` 200×30 (/ desktop n000980) — a sub-brand, not the primary mark. VERDICT: (i)-(iv) and all four stripe marks ARE deterministically whole-host replaceable — the entire `v` is one self-contained mark, and the replacement can reuse `annotateSvgRoot` (src/reconstruction/asset-resolver.ts:225-260, parse5, already strips source class/style/id and stamps `data-wr-node`) so DOM identity survives with NO new attribute. The 184 KB sprite (v) is NOT: it contains 264 `<symbol id>` of which exactly 2 are brand-named (`Linear`, `LinearAi`), nothing `<use>`s them, and replacing the host would destroy every icon on the page — it is an id-rename at most, and `BRAND_SURFACE_POLICY["svg-symbol-id"]` (brand-scan.ts:211-218, "hygiene, not independence") already prices it correctly. So the whole rewrite for linear is a FOUR-entry mark map applied to 48 hosts, and for stripe a FOUR-entry map applied to 108 hosts.

4A REWRITE SEAM — the RSC flight is not optional, PROVEN on real bytes. In data/linear.app/production-builds/2026-08-26T19-26-48-957Z/package/site, the exported `index.html` (2,674,577 B) and the RSC flight `index.txt` (1,293,652 B) BOTH carry the same inline-SVG brand markup, in different encodings. index.html: `aria-label="Linear Logo"` inside `<span class="wr-svg-host"><svg …>` (SSR markup). index.txt: `{"className":"wr-svg-host","dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<svg width=\\"20\\" … aria-label=\\"Linear Logo\\" …` (JSON-escaped). Across the whole package: 50 brand aria-labels in exported HTML vs 32 in the flight `.txt` files, and 32 brand `<symbol id>` in each; 37 flight files, 102 brand-carrying flight chunks. A rewrite that touches only `.html` leaves 64+ flight occurrences intact, and since the inline SVG is delivered as `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` from the flight, the client value wins on hydration mismatch and on any client-side navigation back to the route — the rewrite is REVERTED, exactly as the task brief feared.

4B REWRITE SEAM — worse: the flight is also INLINED INSIDE the HTML, in a THIRD encoding, behind a byte-length prefix. In data/linear.app/production-builds/2026-08-27T09-38-59-704Z/package/site/index.html there are 22 `self.__next_f.push(...)` scripts totalling 1,485,658 of 2,674,090 bytes (55.6% of the file). Splitting the file: `Linear Logo` appears 4× = 2 in SSR markup + 2 inside the inlined flight; `aria-label="Linear` appears 6× in SSR markup and 0× in the flight, while `aria-label=\\"Linear` appears 2× in the flight and 0× in markup. The flight serializes large SVG blobs as LENGTH-PREFIXED raw text chunks: `index.txt` contains `10:Tc20,<svg height="22" viewBox="0 0 400 100" …</svg>` where `c20` = 3104 is the exact byte length of the blob that follows (verified: the blob at offset+3104 ends precisely at `…</path></svg>` and the next chunk id begins immediately after) — 122 such chunks in index.txt, 143 T-chunk markers inside index.html's inlined flight, where the same chunk appears as `10:Tc20,<svg height=\\"22\\" …` (yet another encoding: `<` for `<`). CONSEQUENCE: any post-export byte rewrite that changes a blob's length without recomputing the hex prefix produces a CORRUPT flight payload for the whole route. src/assets/rewrite.ts `applyRewrite` (:32-60) does exactly a length-changing split/join and bake.ts:261-265 runs it over every `.txt`; it has escaped this hazard only by luck — measured: 1132 `/media/` replacements across 37 flight files, 0 of them inside a T-chunk. That is a latent defect Phase 2 must not step on.

4C REWRITE SEAM — the census itself is blind to the flight. src/production/bake.ts:282-304 censuses only `routeHtmlFile(planRoute.route)`; src/production/qa.ts:306-314 censuses only the HTTP body of each route path. Neither ever reads a `.txt` flight file, and `censusServedHtml`'s regexes (`\baria-label\s*=\s*"…"`, brand-census.ts:43) cannot match the flight's `aria-label=\\"…` form even inside the HTML they do read. So an HTML-only rewrite would drive the reported census to 0 while the site still ships the source brand — a false PASS. Phase 2 MUST add a flight-payload axis to the census (a new check, not a weakened one) or its own gate is dishonest.

4D REWRITE SEAM — the seam that has none of these problems already exists and is already used twice. src/production/run.ts:370-379 is the bake pipeline: `copyTemplateApp` (bake.ts:55-65, excludes node_modules/.next/out) → `bakeContent` (bake.ts:72-91) → `bakeTheme` (:94-101) → `bakeSeoTitles` (:104-113) → `convertToStaticExport` (:116-129) → `buildStaticExport` (:131-164). `bakeSeoTitles` READS `<appDir>/reconstruction-data/route-map.json`, MUTATES it via `bakeRouteTitles` (src/production/patch.ts:145-168) and writes it back — before `next build`. patch.ts:135-137 states the reason in one line: "head <title> AND the RSC flight payload both derive from the route table — no string splicing". The same is true of the page IR: the generated app's `load-page.ts` runs `applySlotContent()` on the parsed page before caching, and the generated comment (src/recon-template/app-templates.ts:377-385) says "every render — server HTML and the hydration payload alike — sees the same already-applied tree. There is no client-side patching of any kind." A `bakeBrand(appDir, brandPlan)` mutating `<appDir>/reconstruction-data/pages/*.json` in the COPY, inserted between bake.ts's step C and `convertToStaticExport`, is byte-for-byte the same shape of change as `bakeSeoTitles` and reaches HTML, inlined flight, `.txt` flight and client navigation with ONE write and zero encoding/length arithmetic.

4E REWRITE SEAM — why the asset layer structurally cannot do this. `applyRewrite` is keyed on `sourceUrl` (src/assets/rewrite.ts:32-60, three encodings at :17-24), and the asset serve proxy rewrites html + `text/x-component` + css (src/assets/serve.ts:118-122). An inline SVG has NO url — it is precisely the `entries.filter(e => e.url === null)` population (src/assets/run.ts:172). There is no key to rewrite on. That is the mechanical reason `source-brand-asset` is unreachable from the asset layer, and it is why the `image-logo` policy row (brand-scan.ts:173-180) hands the surface to `replacement-image` while the inline-SVG population has no owner at all. Equally, the content-injection write path cannot reach it: the Slot V2 binding targets are exactly `text | attribute | svg-text` (src/recon-template/types.ts:399) and `applySvgText` (app-templates.ts:265-273) only splices the characters of one addressed `<text>`/`<tspan>` run, guarded by `expectedValue`, with `escapeSvgText` making it impossible to introduce markup. There is no whole-`v` binding target and adding one would bump the Slot V2 schema version — FROZEN.

5 NO-LOGO FALLBACK — today the pipeline renders nothing, and supplying a logo changes zero rendered bytes. `organization-logo` is a `high-value` requirement raised only when the SEO plan omits a JSON-LD `logo` on an injected route (src/release/collect.ts:350-371, SEVERITY_POLICY types.ts:584-587 "JSON-LD logo is omitted honestly when absent"). When an operator DOES supply `assets["organization-logo"]`, src/release/resolve-assets.ts:131-136 takes the site-level branch and logs `"site asset … (recorded; no rewrite target)"` — the file is hashed into `media/<sha256>.<ext>` and recorded, and `consumingStageOfField` returns null for it (requirements.ts:142), so no stage consumes it. `.svg` is already an accepted extension (resolve-assets.ts:25-34). GREP RESULT: there is NO wordmark, monogram, initials or placeholder-logo generation anywhere in src/ or scripts/ — `grep -rni "monogram|wordmark|initials|placeholder-logo|generateLogo"` returns only unrelated `initialState` hits in the interaction detector/explorer. The smallest honest fallback that fits existing conventions: give `organization-logo` a real consumer (4D) and, when no file is supplied, render a TEXT wordmark of the site's own authored name into the host's measured box — the name already exists as `generation-result.json .sitePlan.siteIdentity.workingName` (real value on the linear pilot: "FlowPilot (synthetic-pilot-brand)"). Two honesty caveats: that string carries a parenthetical qualifier and must NOT be rendered blind — Phase 2 needs an explicit `brandName` resolution field or an explicit derivation rule; and a text fallback is a real design change, so it must be recorded as such rather than presented as a neutral no-op. The alternative that invents nothing at all is to leave the host untouched and the requirement unresolved — which is exactly today's dead end, so it is not a fallback, it is the absence of one.

6 FIXTURE FEASIBILITY — a canary is cheap, and a REAL render proof is only ~3 s of `next build`. Three tiers, all honest, none requiring a new source crawl. TIER 1 (pure, milliseconds): copy the existing GED-F fixture shape at scripts/smoke-content-injection.ts:2204-2231 — an `mkdtemp` dir with `template/app/reconstruction-data/route-map.json` + `pages/p000001.json` whose doc carries hand-written nodes — and extend it with the four cases: an inline-SVG wordmark host (`t:"span", v:"<svg viewBox=… aria-label=\"Acme Logo\">…"`), a `<title>Acme logo</title>` host, a 2-symbol sprite host that must SURVIVE untouched, a synthetic `t:"img", p:{src,alt,srcset}` source logo (synthetic is unavoidable — §3B: no real template has one), an `<a aria-label="Acme homepage">`, and a slot-bound text child, plus the `slots.json`/`slot-bindings.json`/`default-content.json` triple. This exercises detection, the IR rewrite and `annotateSvgRoot` identity preservation with no browser and no server. TIER 2 (free, offline, and the only proof of the flight hazard that needs no build at all): assert directly against the existing accepted build data/linear.app/production-builds/2026-08-27T09-38-59-704Z/package/site — that `index.html` and `index.txt` both carry the brand markup, in the three encodings, and that `index.html` carries 143 `T<hex>,` length prefixes. TIER 3 (the real end-to-end proof): the full 8-route linear bake reports `nextBuildMs: 2755` (report/bake-report.json `.build`) and the template app is 56 MB with an 8.1 MB `reconstruction-data`, so a one-route trim + `copyTemplateApp` + `bakeBrand` + `convertToStaticExport` + `next build` is affordable inside a smoke suite; the only expensive part of a full production compile is the media copy (`mediaFilesCopied: 155`, `mediaBytes: 209,680,490`), which a canary avoids with an empty rewrite map. Follow the existing fixture-root convention (`data/.smoke-<name>-<pid>`, scripts/smoke-production.ts:67, removed at :788) and remember the suite mutex — scripts/smoke-release.ts rm -rf's the fixed path data/release-fixture.example.

7 CONSTRAINT FOR PHASE 2 — do not clear the blocker by flipping GED-F. scripts/smoke-content-injection.ts checks 27.brand.8-11 assert `GED_F_NEUTRALIZATION_DEFAULT === false` (:2268-2270), that an explicit `neutralize: true` opt-in still rewrites nothing (:2278-2283), and that the scan leaves every input byte and mtime untouched (:2291). Those checks may not be weakened. The bake-time rewriter must therefore be a SEPARATE mechanism (a `bakeBrand` step driven by an explicit brand-plan artifact) rather than a behaviour change to `scanBrandSurfaces` — which also keeps the detector honest and re-runnable as the verifier of its own rewrite.

options.name: Seam A — bake-time IR transform over the COPIED app's reconstruction-data/pages/*.json
options.howItWorks: Insert a `bakeBrand(appDir, brandPlan)` into src/production/run.ts:370-379 between `bakeSeoTitles` (bake.ts:104-113) and `convertToStaticExport` (bake.ts:116-129), structurally identical to `bakeSeoTitles`: read the JSON in the build copy, mutate, write back, before `next build`. Keyed on a content hash of the normalized `v` markup (mark map) plus (pageId, viewport, nodeId) for prop surfaces. Whole-host SVG replacement re-stamps identity with the existing `annotateSvgRoot` (src/reconstruction/asset-resolver.ts:225-260); img surfaces set p.src/p.alt and delete p.srcset the same way `projectValue` already does (app-templates.ts:88-107); aria-label surfaces are a plain prop write.
options.measured: Reaches 100% of the measured brand surface: template-IR counts reproduce the bake census exactly (48/32/14/2/0 on linear — finding 3A). One write covers SSR HTML, the 1.49 MB of inlined `self.__next_f.push` flight in each HTML, the 37 `.txt` flight files and client-side navigation, because everything derives from the same parsed tree (app-templates.ts:377-385) — the identical argument patch.ts:135-137 already makes for route titles. options.cost: New module + a brand-plan artifact + a new bake step and BakeReport field. Cannot reach anything outside the IR: CSS background images, favicons, `/media` files, and the SEO head (already owned by the SEO plan's brandIsolation gate).
options.risk: Layout: a replacement mark with different intrinsic geometry moves the box — must preserve width/height/viewBox/fill/color from the host and be re-checked by content-injection layout-qa. The 184 KB / 264-symbol icon sprite must be EXCLUDED from whole-host replacement (finding 3C). The build copy is the write target, never the immutable template run.

options.name: Seam B — post-export byte rewrite in postProcessExport (bake.ts:190-330)
options.howItWorks: Extend the existing rewrite loop (bake.ts:237-269) with brand needles, over out/*.html and out/*.txt, the way `applyRewrite` already does for asset URLs.
options.measured: Would have to handle THREE encodings of the same markup (raw SSR, `\"`-escaped in `.txt`, `<`+`\"` in the HTML-inlined flight — finding 4B) AND recompute 122 per-file `T<hexlen>,` byte-length prefixes in index.txt plus 143 in index.html, or corrupt the payload. Measured today: 1132 asset replacements across 37 flight files, 0 inside a T-chunk — the existing code survives only because no asset URL happens to land in one.
options.cost: Small diff, no new artifact, reuses `applyRewrite`.
options.risk: HIGH and structural. A length-changing substitution inside a T-chunk breaks the route's flight parse. Three-encoding coverage is unverifiable by construction. Also cannot preserve SVG root identity (`data-wr-node`) safely with string surgery.

options.name: Seam C — assets serve/rewrite path (src/assets/serve.ts + rewrite.ts)
options.howItWorks: Add the brand marks to the RewriteMap so the proxy/bake asset rewrite neutralizes them.
options.measured: Structurally impossible: `RewriteMap` entries are keyed on `sourceUrl` (rewrite.ts:32-60) and an inline SVG is exactly the population with `url === null` (src/assets/run.ts:172) — 207 of linear's 448 inventory entries. There is no key.
options.risk: n/a — this is the mechanical reason `source-brand-asset` has been unreachable since Task 22, not a candidate.

options.name: Seam D — content-injection write path (slot values / applySvgText)
options.howItWorks: Route the logo through a slot value, the way Task 19.1 routes SVG text.
options.measured: Slot V2 binding targets are exactly `text | attribute | svg-text` (src/recon-template/types.ts:399). `applySvgText` (app-templates.ts:265-273) splices ONE `<text>`/`<tspan>` character run, guarded by `expectedValue`, with `escapeSvgText` deliberately making markup injection impossible. On linear the brand marks are pure `<path>` geometry with `svgText === 0` — there is no run to write. Zero of the 64 brand hosts is reachable.

recommendation: Take Seam A — a bake-time IR transform (`bakeBrand`) over the copied app's `reconstruction-data/pages/*.json`, inserted in src/production/run.ts:370-379 between `bakeSeoTitles` and `convertToStaticExport`.
